title: 0278: mechanism scope CLOSED - the FIRST-MOMENT WALL proves the S-route gate is structurally unreachable; terminal state of route (b)
summary: The 0276 gate (per-piece S-variation c <= cGate, cGate = 2.5821 at tPT2, decaying 1.3445 -> 1.2578 at t3/t4 (0281: landed)) is not a solvable constant-optimization problem: it sits BELOW THE FIRST MOMENT of the thing it bounds. New certified theorem (T4OffLP, 14 strict norm_num theorems + the 0281 t4 completion block, routeBTerminal): every configuration-independent S-route kernel envelope E_win(t) >= dmain(t)*Wspan(t) (mean per-unit zero count x kernel span), while the exclusion needs E_win <= fluc+fedge; at all three profile points the first moment exceeds the requirement (421.61 > 264.2433 at tPT2; 786.62 > 202.6107 at t3; 1259.92 > 250.3585 at t4; ratios 1.596/3.882/5.032 - THE WALL THICKENS, monotone growth (0281 corrected numerals)). The gate constant itself is below the per-unit mean zero count at every point (2.5821 < 4.1199; 1.3445 < 5.2202; 1.2578 < 6.33 (0281: true c*(t4) = 1.2578..1.2704, all sigmas)). No per-piece S-variation bound in the S-route/HSXW/A0c/kind-3 family can reach the gate: the first moment is a lower bound on every sup-form envelope, and a configuration-independent bound cannot see below its own first moment. Empirical confirmation from the known-side data (day081, [1e9,3e9), 2e9 units, 6.2e9 zeros): per-unit zero-count distribution peaks at k=3 (59.0%) and k=4 (25.1%), mean ~3.4, and the observed MAX 2-unit (t-1,t+1] window count is 9 - the landscape sits above the 2.58 gate in mean AND max. The route (b) window-exclusion program is thereby CLOSED as a program (all mechanism classes audited: published 5.00x miss, class kernel 3.2-4.9x, in-machine S-tail 10^12x, spacing-only structural, FIRST-MOMENT WALL certified): the face remains OPEN, the corrected machine is VALID at tPT2/t3/t4, no RH claim.
